dial.summary: BTC dominance has firmed above 60% (60.2% on Oct 18–19) as capital concentrates in Bitcoin ahead of the Oct 28 FOMC decision, with funding rates holding at 0.0100% per 8h — low-leverage accumulation, not speculative excess; macro headwinds persist (DXY 102.07, real yields 2.74%) but Global M2 continues expanding at $103.7T and the Fed balance sheet is flat-to-stable at $6.76T, leaving the macro backdrop mixed rather than deteriorating — no alt-rotation or risk-off triggers in view.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.7T for August 2026 (latest month with all four economies reporting; 4-week trend UP: July $102.64T → August $103.66T, +$1.02T, +1.0% MoM); US M2 at $23.34T for August (FRED H.6, up 5.7% YoY, 28th consecutive monthly increase); September G4 aggregate still unavailable (6–8 week reporting lag); status supportive (4-week trend is up); next full G4 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.5% (released Oct 1, 2026; August 54.6%, 4-week change −0.1pp within flat threshold); ninth consecutive month above 50; New Orders 55.3, Production 56.7, Prices Paid 77.9% (multi-year high); October PMI release scheduled November 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET (confirmed by ISM release calendar); status neutral (above 50 but not rising on 4-week basis).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot at ~102.07 (Oct 19–20, 2026; Trading Economics shows 102.0774 on Oct 19, FXStreet ~101.95 area intraday Oct 19; Oct 16 close ~101.84); 4-week trend UP from ~100.29 on Sep 18 (~+1.8%); 52-week range 95.55–102.95; status headwind (above 100 threshold); FOMC Oct 28 25bp hike to 4.00%–4.25% widely expected, would likely extend DXY toward 103+.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.74% as of October 16, 2026 (Fed H.15, confirmed via Federal Reserve H.15 release page; Oct 15 = 2.78%, Oct 14 = 2.84%, Oct 13 = 2.88% — brief easing from mid-week highs); 4-week trend UP from ~2.52% on Sep 15 to 2.74% (+22bps); status headwind (rising on 4-week basis and above 2% threshold); Oct 20 reading not yet published.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 16, 2026: US 10yr ~5.09%, 2yr ~4.74% → 2s10s spread ~+35bps (FRED T10Y2Y: 0.35 on Oct 16, 0.33 on Oct 15, 0.37 on Oct 14); Oct 19: 10yr at 5.07% (Trading Economics), 2yr not yet confirmed; 4-week trend DOWN (Sep 15 ~+42bps → Oct 16 +35bps = −7bps flattening); status neutral — curve positively sloped but flattening; FOMC Oct 28 hike would compress spread further.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL at ~$6.76T for week ending October 14, 2026 (H.4.1 released Oct 15, 2026; confirmed by Trading Tools citing FRED WALCL; prior week Oct 7 = ~$6.75T, +$8B WoW); 4-week trend flat: Sep 16 ~$6.747T → Oct 14 ~$6.756T = +$9B (+0.13%); status supportive (flat near post-QT-pause stabilization plateau — Reserve Management Purchases offsetting MBS runoff); next H.4.1 release October 22, 2026 (covers week ending Oct 21).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC weighted 8h perp funding rate at ~0.0100% as of October 18–20, 2026 (Tokenpost snapshots Oct 16 and Oct 18 both confirm 0.0100% — highest among the five major perp markets; Alpha Maven Oct 18 = 0.0100% = 10.9% annualized); rate has been stable at this level throughout October; 30-day trend UP from ~0.0067% on Sep 30; well below the 0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (spot-driven accumulation, no speculative leverage excess).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$302.3B (DefiLlama Oct 18–19, 2026; USDT $183.4B, USDC $72.6B; Stablecoin Beat Oct 15 = $303.1B) vs total crypto ~$2.72T (Oct 18–19 range $2.70–2.77T; BTC.D firmed to ~60.2% per TokenPost/TV-Hub Oct 18–19); dominance ~11.1%; 30-day trend UP (Sep 17 est. ~10.5% → Oct 20 ~11.1%); status neutral — stablecoin dominance rising but total crypto market cap is declining (was ~$2.84T late Sep, now ~$2.72T), so the headwind condition (rising dom + rising TOTAL simultaneously) is not triggered.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 18, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended October 18, 2026 — one of the last major labor data points before the October 28 FOMC decision; a sustained trend above 220K would raise recession risk; carries outsized weight given the September NFP of +29K, hot CPI (3.7% YoY), and hot PPI (6.3% YoY) backdrop heading into the meeting.

upcoming.title: Fed Balance Sheet H.4.1 (week ending October 21, 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases weekly H.4.1 balance sheet data (week ending Oct 21) at 4:30 PM ET; prior reading was $6.76T (Oct 14); any acceleration in asset runoff ahead of the Oct 28 FOMC meeting would be notable.

upcoming.title: S&P Global US Flash PMI (October 2026)
upcoming.note: S&P Global releases preliminary October 2026 Manufacturing and Services PMI at 9:45 AM ET — first Q4 activity data point, released four days before the FOMC meeting begins; September ISM Manufacturing at 54.5% sets a high bar; a flash manufacturing print below 52 would suggest deceleration and reinforce Fed hold expectations despite hot inflation.

upcoming.title: UMich Consumer Sentiment Final (October 2026)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan releases the final October 2026 Consumer Sentiment Index at 10:00 AM ET on Friday October 23 — same day as Flash PMI; the preliminary reading typically lands the second Friday of the month (Oct 10), and this final print closes out the pre-FOMC consumer confidence picture ahead of the Oct 27–28 meeting; any sharp downward revision would reinforce stagflation concerns given September CPI at 3.7% YoY and still-elevated mortgage rates.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board releases October 2026 Consumer Confidence Index at 10:00 AM ET — most recent reading was 89.4 (August 2026); released on the same day FOMC Day 1 begins; a sharp drop would reinforce stagflation concerns heading into the Oct 28 decision, while a hold or uptick would reduce pressure on the Fed to slow its hiking pace.

upcoming.title: FOMC Meeting Begins (Day 1 of 2; decision October 28)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve October 2026 FOMC 2-day meeting opens; policy decision and press conference on October 28 at 2:00 PM ET; current Fed Funds target 3.75%–4.00% (raised 25bps on Sep 16, 2026); back-to-back inflation shocks — CPI 3.7% YoY (Oct 14) and PPI 6.3% YoY (Oct 15) — have significantly elevated 25bp hike probability; remaining pre-meeting data: jobless claims (Oct 22), Flash PMI (Oct 23), Consumer Confidence (Oct 27).
